why_prior_verified_refinement_is_not_reu: Dynamic V3 can SELECT an already-proved expensive visible tool before querying an unqueried source that contains a cheaper sufficient tool. Therefore the prior conditional least-cost implication is false even with a complete discovery interface.

formal_lemmas.statement: For any registry state R, gate_invoke accepts only identities in R and discover enumerates exactly R. Therefore every Brain-invocable tool identity is discoverable.
The composed route exposes exactly the owned gateway as the discovery source and V4 emits DISCOVER while it is unqueried. Therefore no PROBE or SELECT precedes complete identity enumeration.

One owned-gateway discovery receipt closes identity enumeration for a stable registry epoch. Thereafter each successful PROBE resolves one previously unknown pair in the finite product of eligible tools and required capabilities.

After complete identity enumeration, eligible tools are traversed by nondecreasing declared cost then opaque identity. A later route is considered only after every earlier route is disproved, so the first selected sufficient route is globally least-cost in the owned invocable universe.
SELECT is emitted only when every required capability for that tool has current positive probe evidence. Hidden capability truth is never read directly.
Registry replacement increments the owned registry epoch. The composition refuses a stale episode before any discovery, probe, selection, or invocation reuse.

A new tool becomes Brain-invocable only by entering a new owned registry epoch. The next episode must rediscover the exact changed registry before selection, preserving unknown/changing-tool support without an external completeness oracle.

For every valid finite owned-registry episode, if an admissible sufficient tool exists the route reaches the globally least-cost such tool after finite evidence acquisition; otherwise it escalates only after no evidence-supported sufficient route remains. Thus terminal-success/valid-route correctness reaches its pointwise ceiling over the declared protocol population.
